# Microbiome Repo — instructions for LLMs and agents
> Evidence-linked metadata for public human microbiome sequencing data — shotgun metagenomes and metatranscriptomes from every body site, all ages: 5,086 projects (INSDC BioProjects), 813,356 samples. Release R2026.44 (package 1.35.0).

Use ONLY the files below; fetch them, do not guess accessions or counts. All files are plain JSON / CSV at stable URLs.

## How to search (do this in order)
1. Choose the most specific selection and fetch it:
   - by intervention the project administered: https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-intervention/<code>.json   (codes: fmt, probiotic, prebiotic_or_fibre, synbiotic, live_biotherapeutic, antibiotic, diet_intervention, dietary_supplement, drug_therapy, surgery, bowel_preparation, exercise, vaccine, phage_therapy, other_intervention)
   - by health condition: https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-condition/<code>.json   (codes in https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/vocabularies.json, e.g. ulcerative_colitis, crohns_disease, ibd_unspecified, colorectal_cancer, type2_diabetes, obesity, healthy_control)
   - by condition term (EFO / MONDO): https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-condition/<anchor>.json   (anchor = the condition id with the colon written as an underscore, e.g. MONDO_0005011.json; 783 of the 785 conditions of the Condition explorer — the rows with no project of their own have no file — listed as endpoints.by_condition_id in https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/index.json and in the `anchor` column of https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/data/conditions/condition_explorer.csv)
   The two are not the same selection: `<code>` counts the catalog's own health-condition code, `<anchor>` counts the samples whose label was mapped to that
   ontology term. Every count inside a project record is the project's own totals, over all its samples, not only the samples of the selection.
   - by age category: https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-age/<neonate|infant|child|adolescent|adult|elderly>.json
   - everything (large, ~2 MB): https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/projects.json
2. Filter the selection's `projects` on the other keys: `health_conditions` (code -> samples), `interventions`, `intervention_design`, `trial_population_condition`,
   `sample_intervention_arms`, `has_cases_and_healthy_controls`, `has_treated_and_control_arms`, `n_samples`, `countries`, `age_categories`, `gbp_per_sample_median`.
3. For each candidate fetch `urls.samples_csv` (https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/samples/<ACCESSION>.csv): one row per sample with sample_key, study_accession, subject_id, timepoint_label, age_category,
   age_at_collection_days, sex, country, health_condition, intervention (this sample's arm), antibiotic_exposure, collection_date, n_runs, seq_gbp.
4. Answer with accessions, sample counts per group/arm, and links (`urls.page`, `urls.ena`). Say when a value is missing rather than inferring it.

## Meaning of the key fields
- `interventions` = what the investigators ADMINISTERED (FMT, probiotic, diet, drug …), project level, read from the abstract / BioProject description. [] = none stated.
- `sample_intervention_arms` / sample column `intervention` = the arm recorded in the archive for that sample; `placebo` and `no_intervention` are the controls / baselines.
- `health_conditions` counts each sample's own condition; `trial_population_condition` is the condition of a trial's participants (e.g. ulcerative_colitis for a UC FMT trial).
- An "IBD + FMT project" = by-intervention/fmt.json filtered to projects whose health_conditions or trial_population_condition include ulcerative_colitis, crohns_disease or ibd_unspecified.

## Worked examples
- "Probiotic trials where both treated and control samples have metagenomes": fetch https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-intervention/probiotic.json; keep projects with
  intervention_design in (randomized_controlled_trial, crossover, non_randomized_controlled) OR has_treated_and_control_arms = true. has_treated_and_control_arms = true
  means the archive labels each sample's arm (best case); for the others read the samples_csv (intervention, timepoint_label, subject_id) and the paper to split arms.
- "Ulcerative colitis FMT projects": fetch https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-intervention/fmt.json; keep trial_population_condition = ulcerative_colitis or health_conditions containing ulcerative_colitis.
- "Adult colorectal-cancer case-control cohorts with healthy controls": fetch https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-condition/colorectal_cancer.json; keep has_cases_and_healthy_controls = true and age_categories containing adult.
- "Infant gut samples from Finland": fetch https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/api/by-age/infant.json; keep countries containing Finland; then read samples_csv.

## For code-running agents
DuckDB can query the full per-sample table over HTTP:
  INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;
  SELECT study_accession, intervention, count(*) FROM read_parquet('https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/data/catalog_sample_metadata_wide.parquet')
  WHERE release_retired IS NULL AND health_condition IN ('ulcerative_colitis','crohns_disease') GROUP BY ALL;
The table keeps the rows retired in earlier releases beside the current ones; `release_retired IS NULL` is the current catalog.
Project-level columns (interventions, intervention_design, population_condition …): https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/data/catalog_studies.parquet. Field definitions: https://microbiome-repo.colorado.edu/fields/index.html.

## Caveats
Values are evidence-linked claims (the archive record wins over the supplementary table, then the paper text, then the abstract), not ground truth; project-level
interventions come from abstracts and may miss arms; every value's evidence is on the project page.
Licence: curated values CC-BY-4.0; archive metadata under INSDC terms; Sandpiper community profiles CC-BY. Cite the primary study of each project as well.
Cite: Microbiome Repo, release R2026.44 (data package 1.35.0), Olm Lab, University of Colorado Boulder, 2026-11-25. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23087712
